verbatim_quote: When planning for family formals, I always suggest leaving 3-5 minutes per photo. If it is a smaller group (maybe 3-6 people), it will be on the lower end of that. If it is a larger group (7-10 people), you will be closer to 5 minutes.
If everything goes well, I can shoot all formals in about 30 minutes.
We like to limit family formals to immediate family so that this portion of the day is limited to 20-25 minutes.
Formals should take around 45 minutes to 1 hour depending on the size of your family and the number of guests. [...] Plan on 3 minutes per group on average.

For most weddings 30 minutes is ideal for family photos, but this is completely dependent on the size of your family! I like to budget 2 minutes for each photo, so if you’d like to keep your family photos to 30 minutes, keep it to 15 photo combinations.

I advise my couples that on average work on 3 to 5 minutes per group. Times this by the ideal number of groups, 6 to 8 and already we have taken 20 to 30 minutes. [...] So, in an ideal world, keep the number of groups to a max of 8 groups.
It will take roughly 2-3 minutes for each group and longer for larger groups more than 8 people. A list of 10-12 group shots will take 20-30mins.
We suggest a maximum of 12 group photos but if you can bring it down to 8, even better! [...] please allow 15-20 minutes in your schedule for the group photos.

country_if_stated: UK (Berkshire and the South of England)
verbatim_quote: For large groups you should allow 5 minutes per group. Smaller groups should be quicker but we are dependent on the timely co-operation of the participants so please do be realistic with your expectations.
Typically, family photoshoots last anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes.

We’ll need about 30 to 45 minutes for family formals (sometimes more, depending on the number of combinations!) and I will send a questionnaire before the wedding where you can list out the shots that you want.
Formals should take around 30 minutes to 40 minutes depending on the size of your family and the number of guests. [...] Plan on 3-4 minutes per group on average.
60 minutes for the first look and couples portraits, 30 minutes for wedding party portraits, and 30 minutes for family portraits.
Plan on four to five minutes per grouping of more than four people. The basic list takes about half an hour. Any groupings beyond that take two to five minutes, depending on size.
I often warn my couples that it takes an average of 2 minutes per image.
A good rule of thumb is to calculate about 3minutes per each family portrait.

When everything is organised, I can usually photograph 10–12 groups in around 20–30 minutes. [...] Around 10–12 core groups works well for many weddings, with up to roughly 15 when there are useful extras.

If you are organised and plan everything you should be able to do the family group shots in under ten minutes, which gives you loads of time to concentrate on getting the candid shots and the complete story of the day.

It's best to keep your group photo list to 10 groupings or less—just your immediate families. [...] Plan for 3 minutes / per grouping of people for these family photos - 30 minutes for 10 different groupings.

Post Ceremony formals normally take around 15-20 minutes depending on the size of your family and the number of guests taking pictures, also the ceremony location may have a set limited time for us to finish. [...] Plan on 3 minutes per group on average.
It can take 3-5 minutes per grouping. [...] The key here is to get the essential group shots (likely around 6-10 groupings), and then move on with your day.

I suggest a handful of poses (read: around fifteen, depending on a few factors) to cover all of our bases with respect to immediate family. [...] The goal here is to put together a list of groupings - and a time slot of twenty minutes or less - that's sure to capture memories you'll appreciate for years & years.
I usually work with my clients to budget 45-50 minutes for family photos, even though it usually doesn't take quite that long.
Allow three minutes per photo and five minutes per photo for groups of ten or more. [...] Please note that 50 minutes should be set aside for this particular session.
As an example, I tell couples to allow 3 minutes per Wedding Formal Combo plus usually around 15 minutes for the Group Photo of the entire Wedding Party.

For groups of 6 people or less you should allow 3 minutes to round up, arrange and take the photo. [...] For larger groups allow for 5 minutes. [...] My aim is to make this part of the day as efficient and easy as possible and to scoot through in about 20-25 minutes, leaving you plenty of time to celebrate with your guests and have a canapes or two. [...] I recommend no more than 10 individual combinations.
Please plan for about 1-4 minutes per photo for shots with fewer than 14 people, about 5-8 minutes per photo for shots with more than 14 people.
Set aside at least 30 minutes for family photos on your wedding day.
I like to allow for 30 mins for most families, though extra large ones may take longer.

Couples who want to built in stress-free, FUN group shots should schedule 30-45 minutes. If you're keeping them between 8-10 manageable group combinations this time frame should allow ample opportunity for your photographer to work through them as EFFICIENTLY as circumstance allows.
A dozen or fewer are ideal [...] A dozen groups is an ideal number, to cover all the important combinations, and still keep everyone on-board.
Keep your group photos list to around 6-8 groups MAX! [...] We shoot them 10-15 minutes before you sit down for food/speeches… and the whole process doesn’t take longer than 10 minutes!
We suggest thirty minutes for family portraits.

Usually I say family photos should take about 20-30 mins depending on the number of groupings. If you require more then about 10 groupings then additional time will be needed which will affect your timeline slightly.

Book family photo slots right after the ceremony, 15 to 25 minutes, with a pre-written list of 8 to 12 groupings. [...] Write a family photo list and cap it at 8 to 12 groups [...] If portraits with family are important, budget 3 to 4 minutes per group of 6 to 10 people.

Once you have this list figured out, and we recommend 10-15 groups max, arrange it from largest groupings down to smallest (per family) and include your names too [...] There is typically only 1-hour between ceremony and reception to capture family photos (2-3 minutes per grouping, ~30-35 minutes for 15 groups), wedding party photos (if there was no first look prior), and Couples Photos (~20 minutes).
As a rough idea, I’d expect the above number of photographs to take approx 20-30mins.

6-10 formal groups is sufficient to capture immediate family and very close friends, including a shot of the entire group of people if the venue allows for a shot that will include everyone [...] Imagine that gathering the people for 10 groups may take 3 minutes per group, you need to allow half an hour for 10 groups shots.

It’s probably good to keep this shot list to a maximum of 15 combinations because any more than that, and you’ll start to get exhausted. Trust me on this one. I typically allot 20-30 minutes for family photos, so if you’re wanting more shots than this (such as adding extended family photos) you’ll need to plan for extra time.
